Changelog

Each release leads with one change, then a few fixes.

v2.3.172026-11-16

Delegated sub-tasks are more dependable: dropped streams and errors retry on their own, and the files they changed come back to the main chat. Click a file mentioned in the chat to open it in the side pane.

  • Resend a step automatically when the model's reply breaks before any tool ran (dropped stream, connection reset, server 5xx, 429 and similar), up to 5 times with growing delays. Auth, quota and context-length errors are not retried.
  • Retry a delegation automatically on transient errors or when the coding assistant crashes mid-run, up to 5 times. If a background delegation still fails, Nomi takes over while the chat is idle, with another coding assistant or on its own.
  • Bring a sub-task's changed files back to the main chat: the result lists each file with lines added and removed, with the same "Edited N files" card as the sub-task pane underneath, so you can open each diff.
  • Keep talking to sub-agents that Nomi sent out: opening a delegation from session details opens its own coding-assistant tab, where you can continue the conversation.
  • Open relative file links and path-like inline code in the chat in the side pane instead of the system browser.
  • Animate the side tabs, the preview pane and the built-in browser when switching and going fullscreen. A sliding indicator moves between tabs, and settings and segmented controls use the same one.
  • Line the sub-task tabs on the right up with the main chat again: in split view the tab row sits back in the title bar, and the conversation top and the composer bottom match the main chat.

Details

  • Agent requests with tools retry 5 times by default, and an unfinished plan that keeps making progress is nudged forward, up to 8 times.
  • A tab whose last task failed is no longer reused for new delegations. Errored or stopped delegation tabs stay open so you can keep replying, and are tidied up after a week idle like other finished tabs. Failed or stopped runs also bring back the files they already edited and name the folder the changes landed in.
  • Follow-up turns in a sub-task and files that already had changes before the delegation are now included in the changes brought back.
  • Agents in session details are grouped by status: running, failed, then done, newest first in each group. Icons and names on tabs, in session details and on hover cards follow the sub-agent's real source.
  • Side chats, open files and preview tabs are remembered per session, and move over once a new coding-assistant tab gets its session.
  • The file tree on the open-file and changes pages can be collapsed, and the choice is remembered.
  • The built-in browser detects pages that refuse to be embedded and pages that never finish loading.
  • File lookup by name skips node_modules, vendor, dist and similar folders.

v2.3.162026-11-16

When you open Nomi again, the brand splash no longer stays up. Agents in session details follow live status, and ↑ in an empty composer brings back the question you just sent.

  • The brand splash closes within 8 seconds when you open Nomi again. Skip animation closes it at once, and conversations and the sidebar keep loading behind it.
  • Agents in session details follow live status: a sub-task is listed as running as soon as it appears in the current turn. After an error, continuing in that sub-task shows it running again, then the result of that follow-up. A background sub-agent that is still running after a coding-assistant turn ends keeps its live status.
  • Press ↑ in an empty composer to recall the question you just sent.
  • The session details button now sits next to the button that shows or hides the tab row (4 px apart), so it no longer covers it. On macOS the extra gap of about 40 px is gone. On Windows and Linux it stays to the left of minimize, maximize, and close.
  • The sidebar usage card no longer shows the coding assistant's name; it keeps the colored icon and the same badges. The name is still in the details.

Details

  • Each startup task waits at most 5 seconds, and fonts at most 1.5 seconds. If the window is hidden and layout frames do not run, the splash still closes on a timer. Starting a new conversation or clearing one during startup no longer leaves the splash waiting for history.
  • The usage card's name is still read by screen readers, and it remains in the details you open.

v2.3.152026-11-15

Changes and files can each open as their own tab, long conversations can be jumped by turn, and with Nomi set to Auto, allowed actions no longer ask again.

  • Changed and Open file are separate closable tabs, alongside sub-tasks and file previews. The title-bar control shows or hides the whole tab row (⌘⇧B on macOS, Ctrl+Shift+B on Windows and Linux) without discarding tab state. + opens a New tab page where you can search files or type a URL, or open Browser, Files, Changed, and Side chat; opening one replaces that New tab. The in-app browser opens the page inside the tab, accepts only http and https, and switches to the system browser when a site refuses to be embedded.
  • When a conversation already has more than five assistant replies, a quick navigator appears on the left. Click a mark to jump to that turn, and hover to read a summary of the reply. Scrolling to the top keeps loading earlier messages; jumping to a turn that is not loaded yet loads only up to that turn.
  • Clicking the session name in the title bar opens the existing session menu, and you can change this session's Transcript view. On Windows and Linux the title bar leaves room for minimize, maximize, and close.
  • After first-run setup, Nomi opens the workbench and leaves the desktop character off until you turn it on in Settings → General → Startup & windows. Role and interests are compact tags, and the description appears after you select one. Startup draws the brand mark first: onboarding tucks it into the top-left corner, and later launches wait until conversations are ready. You can skip it; it does not play when reduced motion is on.
  • With Nomi's permission set to Auto, allowed actions run directly, including deletions and other destructive actions, and writes after this turn has read outside content. Workspace limits, sensitive paths, and actions that need extra system consent still follow their own rules. Switch back to Auto-edit files or Ask each time when you want a check on every step.
  • A coding assistant handed work while Nomi is on Auto uses the highest mode that assistant supports, and never Full access. Without an OS sandbox, ordinary background tasks still confirm commands one by one; only an assistant that Nomi explicitly delegates while on Auto runs automatically.
  • After you choose Always run in this chat, that command and other ordinary commands in the same conversation and the same working directory no longer ask. Credential, external, and irreversible commands still ask every time. A different directory, a different conversation, or a restart asks again.

Details

  • On Auto-edit files, commands still go through command review. After outside content is read, or when review rejects the command or cannot run, Nomi stops to ask.
  • Without a working directory, Files and Changed on the New tab page stay unavailable. Once you have opened the tab area, it stays open when you switch to a session that has no tabs yet; it closes only after you close the last tab.
  • Settings open inside the workbench, and going back keeps the composer draft and scroll position. Sidebar icons and the changes list were tidied.
  • On Windows, different spellings of the same working directory (drive-letter case, slashes, a trailing slash) count as one directory.

v2.3.142026-11-14

The right side is now a tabbed workspace for several agents and files at once. Scheduled tasks and delegated coding assistants can also run with risk-based review; without an OS sandbox, commands still need confirmation one by one.

  • Opening a sub-agent or a file adds a tab on the right. Several can stay open, each with its live state. Tabs can be reordered, maximized, split, or popped out. A hover card is available, and a text selection can be added to the conversation or asked about in a side chat; more than one side chat can be open.
  • The sub-agent sidebar now matches the main pane.
  • Pinning a conversation keeps it first inside the current project, instead of moving it outside the project.
  • The Dynamic Island notifies once when a task finishes. When the workbench is already on screen, only items that need your action or an alert appear.
  • Third-party CLI models use the same thinking depth as the main conversation. Local assistant sign-in and the "external CLI" entry are gone.
  • Scheduled tasks: with a grant of L3 ("can run commands") or higher and an OS sandbox available, commands go to command review and run once cleared. Only high-risk steps, credential reads, never-allow classes, review rejections, and actions after reading outside content still stop to ask. Without an OS sandbox (including on Windows), L3 does not auto-run commands; they stay on per-command confirmation, while file edits can still happen automatically. "Judge by risk" and foreground "full auto" also will not auto-run commands in that case. "Judge by risk" is checked by default when creating a task; uncheck it to be asked about every command.
  • Delegated coding assistants (such as Codex): finished work is accepted automatically, changes are landed in the working tree, and the result returns to the conversation. Background tasks also follow risk-based review; without an OS sandbox, commands are not auto-approved.
  • Command review sends the full command to the review model. Common secrets, tokens, and the home directory are redacted first, but redaction cannot catch every secret.
  • Recurring tasks return to "waiting for trigger" after each run instead of getting stuck on "awaiting acceptance".
  • Messages to a sub-agent can only go to a discovered child of the current tab; the main thread and unregistered ids are rejected.

Details

  • Workspace authorization errors in the preview stay visible instead of flashing by.
  • Diff drafts survive switching preview tabs, and saves check the revision first so they do not overwrite outside changes.
  • The unused "Agents in this session" item is gone from the + menu; the Agents list in session details remains.

v2.3.132026-11-13

When a decision is needed, a question card appears above the composer; you can also choose a thinking depth for each model.

  • Nomi, Claude Code, Codex and ACP questions are answered on this card: lettered options, free text, multi-select or skip. Stop, emergency stop, closing the session, or a timeout ends the question.
  • Thinking depth lives in the model chip and only appears for models that can think. The default is the second tier in that model's own list.
  • Context is compacted at each model's standard window, defaulting to 256K. Unrecognized models also use 256K, no longer 128K.
  • Coding-assistant detection no longer stays on “Checking…”: local install state is shown as soon as the probe finishes, and latest versions refresh in the background (#350).

Fixes

  • Conversation titles are generated as soon as you send, and the sidebar and preview show running state.
  • Diff draft saves check the revision first so they do not overwrite outside changes. A failed save keeps the draft.
  • Opening Computer Use settings on Windows no longer pops command consoles repeatedly.

v2.3.122026-11-12

The workbench is no longer split into Chat and Workshop; coding-agent UI stays visible once those tools are installed.

  • The sidebar top row is a full-width New chat button; only Settings remains at the bottom left. Knowledge and Extensions still open from the composer menu or shortcuts.
  • Gemini no longer offers Google account sign-in. Upgrading deletes Gemini accounts and credentials saved in Nomi; it does not change ~/.gemini in your terminal.
  • Computer Use screenshots and visual targeting skip blocked apps; the emergency stop also cancels a turn that has already been running.
  • Unsaved edits in a Diff preview tab are kept when you switch tabs, and closing the tab asks first. The first “New task” from the command palette opens the create form.

Fixes

  • “Use the terminal proxy” now lives only under Settings → Coding agents → General.
  • Icon buttons no longer show native tooltips; their names come from accessibility labels.
  • The in-app word 智能体 is now Agents.

Older releases are on GitHub Releases.
